description: The settings window, by the label SETTINGS_WINDOW in src/settings_window.rs; rename both together (docs/decisions/0028-settings-window.md). Grants nine bridge commands, one permission each: dispatch and query (the bridge admits only SetUiSettings, SetToolSettings, SetPrivacySettings, SetSkillPack, AddSkill (only a path pick_skill returned), RemoveSkill, RefreshLimits, SetUpdateMode, CheckForUpdate, the connector commands Check, Add, AddApiKey, AddCredits, SignOut, Remove and RefreshBalance (never DismissCaseLawHint, the room's), GetSettings and GetUpdate from this window; src/bridge/admit.rs), open_stream, subscribe_app and ack for its channel and the app feed, display_info, and setup for Plans (docs/decisions/0048-signin-on-the-wire.md; src/setup/admit.rs admits every setup action from this window), pick_skill, the folder dialog of Skills' Add a skill (src/commands/pick.rs), and quit_app, which takes no arguments and quits the app as Cmd+Q does, through the stop steps and the sign-in cancel, for the Get the installer button (src/commands.rs). Beside them, permissions and ask_permission, the first-start permissions step's list and its Ask button (src/permissions.rs; each only reads what the OS allows, or asks through the OS's own dialog). Settings shows the same Permissions block for a lawyer who already has matters and never sees the first screen; the OS prompt rises only when the lawyer presses Allow there, as on the first screen. And only the two window commands of Tauri's drag script, DRAG_PERMISSIONS in src/window_frame.rs, and set_title, so the page names its window in the app's language (TITLE_PERMISSION in src/settings_window.rs); capabilities/frame.json adds the caption buttons' on Windows and Linux. Never subscribe, unsubscribe, answer_permission, pick_folder, pick_folder_or_choose, chooser_starts, chooser_list, chooser_choose, chooser_cancel, chooser_shown, open_external, open_file, reveal or open_settings: every permission widens what script in the page can reach.
